title: HF513 (2021-2022 Regular): Right to carry without a permit provided, and optional permit to carry provided.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2021-01-28; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/92/2021/0/HF/513/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version, 2021-01-28. No votes recorded. Section 9 repeals Minn. Stat. 624.714, subds. 1a, 1b, 16 and 624.7181 (rifles and shotguns in public places); the repealed text is in the appendix and not quoted. Section 1(a) is a legislative declaration about the Second Amendment, not quoted. Sections 4, 6, 7 change application, database and reporting wording from 'permit holders' to people carrying under the section.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 1c): (b) A person who is not prohibited from possessing a firearm by any law of this state or any federal law shall have the right to carry, hold, or possess a firearm in a motor vehicle, snowmobile, or boat, or on or about the person's clothes or the person, or otherwise in possession or control in a public place.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 1d): A person may apply for an optional permit to carry a pistol as provided in this section.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 2): (b) Unless a sheriff denies a permit under the exception set forth in subdivision 6, paragraph (a), clause (3), a sheriff must issue a permit to an applicant if the person: (1) has training in the safe use of a pistol; (2) is at least 21 years old and a citizen or a permanent resident of the United States; (3) completes an application for a permit;
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 2): (c) A permit to carry a pistol issued or recognized under this section is a state permit and is effective throughout the state.
Section 8 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 23): No sheriff, police chief, governmental unit, government official, government employee, or other person or body acting under color of law or governmental authority may change, modify, or supplement these criteria or procedures, or limit the exercise of the right to carry a firearm.
